FR-001.title: The active controller receives eligible target feedback by the next animation frame without waiting for the network.

FR-002.title: Controller-local transient presentation remains visual-only and non-authoritative.

FR-003.title: Local transient presentation is keyed so older revisions cannot overwrite newer pointer intent.

FR-004.title: Shared presentation, observer rendering, and preview audio remain authoritative.

FR-005.title: The client retains only the newest distinct unsent semantic presentation target and suppresses duplicates.

FR-006.title: Delayed updates do not replay superseded effects and all views converge on the final target.

FR-007.title: The system exposes an optional generated protobuf client-streaming presentation operation without browser bidi.

FR-008.title: Subscribe remains authoritative and carries tab-targeted presentation results or rejections.

FR-009.title: Each tab uses an ephemeral client identity and explicit uplink generation.

FR-010.title: Every presentation intent identifies its request, player, broadcast, terminal, context, and semantic target.

FR-011.title: The server revalidates authority and context for every stream intent.

FR-012.title: Each uplink maintains a capacity-one latest-value mailbox.

FR-013.title: Accepted presentation mutations preserve coordinator and revision ordering.

FR-014.title: Targeted results cannot disturb or broadcast canonical revision delivery.

FR-015.title: The authenticated public request stream reaches both local hops over HTTP/2.

FR-016.title: Player server and ingress retain HTTP/1.1 compatibility.

FR-017.title: Streaming is enabled only after capability detection and a successful end-to-end probe.

FR-018.title: Unsupported or failed streaming paths fall back automatically to unary presentation.

FR-019.title: SetPresentation remains available and preserves BUG-010 bounded unary behavior.

FR-020.title: Whole-request buffering is bypassed only for PresentationUplink.

FR-021.title: The stream retains host, origin, authentication, size, decompression, and schema protections.

FR-022.title: The system enforces stream rate, lifetime, concurrency, cancellation, and shutdown limits.

FR-023.title: Invalid or slow streams cannot mutate state or disrupt healthy clients.

FR-024.title: Authority, context, generation, reconnect, and shutdown changes invalidate obsolete streaming state.

FR-025.title: Other gameplay mutations remain unary and behaviorally unchanged.

FR-026.title: Session and player-configuration formats remain unchanged.

FR-027.title: Public presentation contracts remain free of private capabilities and secrets.

FR-028.title: Public access failure does not prevent local or LAN access.

FR-029.title: The ngrok tunnel requests HTTP/2 with the required upstream option.

FR-030.title: The browser stream uses Fetch ReadableStream and generated protobuf contracts without handwritten network DTOs or routing.

context: areas: player transport, tunnel ingress, protobuf contract, browser presentation
constraint: optional stream with generated messages and portable unary fallback
constraint: canonical state, observer rendering, revisions, and preview audio remain authoritative
intent: Reduce controller-visible presentation latency with safe local feedback and an optional bounded HTTP/2 uplink while preserving authoritative convergence and unary fallback.
expectations: Do not convert other gameplay mutations to streams.
Do not add browser bidi, WebSocket, or WebTransport.
Do not change persistent session or player-configuration formats.
Do not replace Subscribe as the authoritative downlink.
approach: Add an optional generated PresentationUplink bound to the current physical Subscribe, with capacity-one latest intent processing and targeted downlink results. Enable native Go 1.27 h2c through ngrok and ingress, while a generated-descriptor Fetch transport uses local visual transients and falls back to BUG-010 unary dispatch.

decisions.decision: Use Go 1.27 net/http Protocols for HTTP/1.1 plus h2c on both servers
decisions.why: The standard library directly supports unencrypted HTTP/2 and preserves one listener
decisions.rejected: Deprecated x/net/http2/h2c wrapper or a second listener

decisions.decision: Use a generated-descriptor Fetch ReadableStream wrapper only for PresentationUplink
decisions.why: Connect-Web rejects browser request streaming but exports official framing helpers and the exact versions are pinned
decisions.rejected: Handwritten envelopes/router or replacing the ordinary Connect transport

decisions.decision: Prove the open request through a targeted ready result on Subscribe
decisions.why: The independent downlink proves an uplink frame crossed every intermediary before request EOF
decisions.rejected: JavaScript capability checks, unary health checks, or reading an open upload response

decisions.decision: Keep canonical and targeted subscription delivery in separate bounded queues
decisions.why: Targeted statuses and results cannot consume, reorder, evict, or overflow-close canonical revisions
decisions.rejected: One shared queue or blocking targeted delivery

decisions.decision: Retain BUG-010 unary dispatch as automatic fallback
decisions.why: Browser and deployment request streaming is non-portable and local/LAN HTTP must remain functional
decisions.rejected: Removing unary or sending one target through both transports

decisions.decision: Supersede the earlier targeted-result mailbox decision: keep it capacity-one and non-lossy; only the originating uplink processor waits for result capacity or cancellation, without blocking canonical delivery or holding coordinator locks.
decisions.why: Processed targeted rejections/results must reach the active tab while canonical revision delivery remains isolated.
decisions.rejected: Replacing or silently dropping processed results; blocking the canonical queue or coordinator.

plan.summary: Planned generated client-stream presentation with local transient feedback, bounded tab routing, native h2c, and unary fallback.
plan.key_finding: Connect-Web 2.1.2 intentionally rejects request streams, so the safe browser path is a narrow generated-descriptor wrapper over official Connect framing helpers.
plan.risks: Cross-tab binding, canonical/result queue isolation, intermediary buffering, and stale visual/audio reconciliation require race and browser stress coverage.

tasks.summary: 38 dependency-ordered tasks across Setup, Foundational, three prioritized user-story phases, and Polish; each implementation wave is preceded by focused RED tests and followed by explicit joins.
tasks.key_finding: Client and server latest-only mailboxes plus non-lossy starvation-free targeted delivery require distinct bounded queues and single-owner processors.
tasks.risks: Browser request-stream support, cross-tab generation binding, HTTP/2 hop proof, targeted backpressure, and stale visual/audio reconciliation require race and Playwright stress coverage.
